columns:
A contract under which one party (the insurer) accepts significant insurance risk from another party (the
policyholder) by agreeing to compensate the policyholder if a specified uncertain future event (the insured event)
adversely affects the policyholder or, in the case of life annuities, the lifespan of the policyholder is greater than that
assumed. Such contracts may also transfer financial risk. The group defines significant insurance risk as the possibility
of having to pay benefits on the occurrence of an insured event that are significantly more than the benefits payable
if the insured event did not occur.
